A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAM2Act/SAM2Act+ research. All pages, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–I support comparison; v4's additional page results from reflow and expanded references.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulation and real-robot experiments in Section 5, with detailed benchmark results and ablations in Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v4 retains the original SAM2Act/SAM2Act+ simulation, real-robot and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: Section 4, Algorithm 1 and Appendix A retain the same SAM2 encoder adaptation, multi-resolution upsampling, multi-view transformer and action-memory architecture. The newly discussed relational-memory approach belongs to cited prior work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 18 RLBench tasks, 20 Colosseum tasks with 13 perturbation categories, three MemoryBench tasks and four real-world tasks. Task descriptions in Appendices F–I are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix comparisons, including Tables 1–4, 7 and 9. The three newly cited works are discussed in related work but are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The splits, demonstration counts, trial counts, metrics, training budgets and single-task/multitask settings are unchanged. Appendix H's drawer-waypoint modification, retraining and memory-window update already appear in v3.

E4.justification: Appendix E and Tables 2 and 9 retain the same encoder substitutions and upsampling ablations. The simulated perturbation tests and real-world generalization analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four evaluations for RLBench/MemoryBench and three for The Colosseum, retaining the same standard-deviation reporting. No run-count, seed or statistical-estimation changes are introduced.

E6.justification: Reported results and rankings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Examples include 86.8±0.5% RLBench success in Table 1, −4.3±3.6% Colosseum change in Table 2 and 94.3±9.0% MemoryBench success in Table 3.

T1.justification: The Markov-property formulation in Section 3.1 and mathematical definitions of multi-resolution upsampling in Section 4.1 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about precision, generalization, spatial memory and MemoryBench. Their headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of the experiments and ablations are retained. Section 6 preserves the limitations concerning dexterous continuous control, task-dependent memory windows and semantic-memory retention; the added passages instead summarize prior research.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain the same architecture specifications, sampling procedures, checkpoint-selection information, GPU descriptions and hyperparameters in Tables 5–6. Project-site and implementation-access statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds two works on object-centric representations by Shi et al. and Qian et al. Section 2.3 adds Huang et al.'s Out of Sight, Still in Mind and describes its tracking-enabled relational memory. These are limited expansions of research positioning; existing references are retained.

P1.justification: Sections 2.2–2.3 receive localized prose additions and connective wording changes. The remaining narrative, section order and appendix organization are retained, with updated citation numbering and arXiv version/date text.

P2.justification: Text reflow changes placement, notably moving Table 2 from page 9 in v3 to page 10 in v4 and shifting the appendices one page later. The five figures and eleven tables retain their graphics, structure and substantive captions.

improvement.justification: The additions in Sections 2.2–2.3 acknowledge relevant object-centric representation and tracking-based memory research omitted from v3, making the research positioning more complete. The method, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall quality gain is limited.
